title: How Dagobert Renouf grew his startup with Twitter story tweets, not ads
summary: Dagobert explains how a failed paid-ads attempt pushed him to organic Twitter. He covers why Twitter has no reach ceiling, why personal story tweets beat memes and guru one-liners, and why a face-and-name account beats a brand account. He also covers engaging first to get shown and how a small audience can still pay off.

principles.text: Pick Twitter over Indie Hackers because its reach has no ceiling; focus there and it keeps compounding.
principles.quote: Twitter the ceiling is kind of infinite so that's what convinced me to focus on Twitter instead

principles.text: Turn events into a problem-and-solution story with a lesson, not a flat status update.
principles.quote: if you can transform that into today I had this problem then I found this solution and now this gives me hope for XYZ then it's like 10 times more powerful

principles.text: Drop the guru one-liners; share your own experience for more humility, authenticity and traction.
principles.quote: instead of trying to make a big sentence that teaches people everything I was like let's just start with I like I experiened this today like this happened to me way simpler way more humility and way more authentic

principles.text: Personal story tweets convert viewers to followers better than memes, which get laughs but no curiosity.
principles.quote: when you write a story that's more personal then they're curious and that's I think the core of my you know quote unquote success on Twitter it's actually the story tweets

principles.text: Build the account on your real face and name; people bond with people more than with brands.
principles.quote: there's nothing better than using your face your name um and being the most uh authentic you can be about who you are

principles.text: To get early likes, engage with people you resonate with first; Twitter then shows your tweets to them.
principles.quote: you have to engage first like you basically have to start engage with other people
